images.note: Beat: fragile banks, no deposit insurance - 'a bank didn't get rescued. It failed' - 5,000 banks closed by 1932, five million Americans lost savings. Front page of the Washington Times, Mar 6, 1933: 'NATION PREPARES FOR USE OF SCRIP - Banks to Reopen for Limited Service' (the national bank holiday). DATING NOTE: March 1933 is just past the lesson's 1932 frame, but this is the culminating image of the banking collapse the script describes; kept with the date stated plainly. Served at 1466px wide; headline visually confirmed on a preview render. alt_url null: no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px 1930-32 bank-run image (LOC's Bank of United States run photo serves max 640px; the famous alternatives are rights-managed).

images.note: Beat: Smoot-Hawley - 'gasoline, not the spark.' In 1930 Congress raised tariffs to near-record highs; other countries retaliated; world trade collapsed; it made a downturn global. Front page of the Washington Daily News, June 17, 1930 (signing day): 'PRESIDENT SIGNS TARIFF BILL' with portraits of the principals - Smoot and Hawley visible - and 'Hawley and Smoot Are Present at Simple Ceremonies Attending Signing at White House.' Contemporary, period-true. Served at 1460px wide; headline and portraits visually confirmed on a preview render. alt_url null: no second institution yielded a verifiable >=1200px tariff image (LOC's April 1929 Smoot/Hawley portrait serves max 640px).
images.title: Washington Daily News front page, June 17, 1930 - 'President Signs Tariff Bill' (Smoot-Hawley)
